blocks.prompt: 12 If between any two numbers there are inserted two A.Ms. \(A_1, A_2\), two G.Ms. \(G_1, G_2\) and two H.Ms. \(H_1, H_2\); show that \(\frac{A_1 + A_2}{G_1 G_2} = \frac{H_1 + H_2}{H_1 H_2}\).
blocks.explanation:
A proof. Call the two numbers \(a\) and \(b\).
In a 4-term A.P. (or G.P.) the two middle terms add (or multiply) to the same as the two ends.
Plan: show both sides equal \(\frac{a + b}{ab}\).
steps:
Given: \(a, A_1, A_2, b\) in A.P.; \(a, G_1, G_2, b\) in G.P.; \(a, H_1, H_2, b\) in H.P. (\(a, b\) positive).
To prove: \(\frac{A_1 + A_2}{G_1 G_2} = \frac{H_1 + H_2}{H_1 H_2}\).
Method: Use the "equidistant terms" property of A.P. and G.P., and apply the A.P. property to the reciprocals of the H.P.

Sum of the A.M.s
\[A_1 = a + d, \quad A_2 = b - d\]
\[A_1 + A_2 = a + b\]
Why: In the A.P. \(a, A_1, A_2, b\), \(A_1\) is one step after \(a\) and \(A_2\) one step before \(b\); the \(d\)s cancel.

Product of the G.M.s
\[G_1 = ar, \quad G_2 = \dfrac{b}{r}\]
\[G_1 G_2 = ab\]
Why: In the G.P. \(a, G_1, G_2, b\), \(G_1\) is one step (×\(r\)) after \(a\) and \(G_2\) one step before \(b\); the \(r\)s cancel.

So the left side is
\[\dfrac{A_1 + A_2}{G_1 G_2} = \dfrac{a + b}{ab}\]
Why: Put the sum on top and the product below.

Use the A.P. of reciprocals for the H.M.s
\[\dfrac{1}{a}, \; \dfrac{1}{H_1}, \; \dfrac{1}{H_2}, \; \dfrac{1}{b} \text{ in A.P.}\]
\[\dfrac{1}{H_1} + \dfrac{1}{H_2} = \dfrac{1}{a} + \dfrac{1}{b}\]
Why: Same property as for \(A_1 + A_2\): middle pair sum = end pair sum.

Write both sides as single fractions
\[\dfrac{H_1 + H_2}{H_1 H_2} = \dfrac{a + b}{ab}\]
Why: \(\frac{1}{H_1} + \frac{1}{H_2} = \frac{H_2 + H_1}{H_1 H_2}\) and \(\frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} = \frac{b + a}{ab}\).

Conclude
\[\dfrac{A_1 + A_2}{G_1 G_2} = \dfrac{a + b}{ab} = \dfrac{H_1 + H_2}{H_1 H_2}\]
Why: Both sides equal the same fraction.
Check with \(a = 1, b = 8\): A.P. 1, 3, 6, 8 gives \(A_1 + A_2 = 9\); G.P. 1, 2, 4, 8 gives \(G_1 G_2 = 8\); and \(\frac{1}{H_1} + \frac{1}{H_2} = 1 + \frac{1}{8} = \frac{9}{8}\). Both sides are \(\frac{9}{8}\) \(\checkmark\).
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\frac{A_1 + A_2}{G_1 G_2} = \frac{H_1 + H_2}{H_1 H_2}\) (both equal \(\frac{a + b}{ab}\)).
